title: Weekly POC: Private pilot telemetry & routing debrief
summary: Weekly sync to review telemetry from the Private pilot (VPC/on-prem), recent routing changes, kernel upgrade plan, and next steps for a controlled rollforward. Discussed packet drops on egress path, audit log retention, and a small perf regression after the quant kernel swap; agreed to run an e2e benchmark and a narrow canary next weekend.
next_steps: Priya: run 1k-concurrency e2e benchmark with both pre/post kernel bundles and share results by 2025-10-27
Jordan: send updated network diagram including egress NAT and peering IPs by 2025-10-24
Leah: provide list of required audit log fields and retention policy constraints by 2025-10-24
Samir & Priya: coordinate small canary on 2025-11-01 (2-hour maintenance window), final decision by 2025-10-30
action_items: Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Investigate 5% token-level latency spike when switching to quant-kernel v2 and submit a short RCA by 2025-10-26
Jordan Meyers (AE): Share pilot pricing delta for dedicated fallback capacity and updated SOW stub by 2025-10-28
Samir Khan (NimbleHealth): Validate VPC route table entries and confirm NAT GW throughput headroom by 2025-10-24
Leah Ortiz (NimbleHealth): Confirm KMS/HSM key rotation windows with security team and share constraints by 2025-10-29
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 50m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Carlos (Redwood) — Ruth, Samir, Leah, Tom (NimbleHealth)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining on time, quick agenda — telemetry review, routing incidents, kernel plan, and next steps. Ruth, Samir, anything to add?

[00:15] Ruth (NimbleHealth): thanks Jordan, nothing big to add, mainly we saw a couple of anomalies in the past 48 hours on the pilot traffic, some increased tail latency and a couple of 502s when we started the batch load tests.

[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): got it, we're going to walk through the traces — quick note, some of the log names may appear as "red wood-private" in the exporter, the downstream service names are getting munged, sorry if the auto-parse is messy.

[00:45] Tom (NimbleHealth): yeah the traces look noisy, also noticed TLS handshake errors in a few traces, could be MTU or an intermediate proxy.

[01:05] Samir (Infra): we didn't change proxies but we had a firewall policy update last night to tighten egress. Could be that, also we have a NAT gateway at 10Gb that might be pegged during the batch.

[01:20] Priya: okay let's pull up the telemetry dashboard — (screen share) — so here's requests-per-second and p50/p95; you can see at 02:14 UTC there was a spike in p99 and then a number of retries which caused a short burst of 5xx responses. The traces indicate a handful of retransmits and then the automatic fallback route triggered to the hosted model variant.

[01:45] Ruth: fallback happened automatically? that seems risky for data residency — we need to ensure fallback never leaves the VPC for certain tenants.

[02:00] Jordan: yep good point — current fallback policy is "best-effort" to preserve availability; we can change the policy to fail closed for tenants that require strict residency. That is configurable per-route.

[02:20] Leah (Security): we need SLOs and an assurance that fallback won't egress for regulated data; plus we need proof that audit logs contain the decision and the fallback path. What fields are you logging?

[02:35] Priya: we log route_decision, model_variant, region, and whether KV-cache hit was used. I think the audit exporter strips some headers right now — there's a gap where the decision_id isn't persisted in long-term logs. We'll add that as an action.

[02:55] Samir: also to call out, the 502s correlated with a small MTU mismatch on the on-prem gateway. We saw fragmented packets from the model-serving NIC, so the kernel upgrade PR changed some TCP offload flags which affected frag handling.

[03:20] Priya: oh interesting — that matches the change we pushed: quant-kernel v2. The performance wins are good but we did see a small regression in tail latency for long sequences in one config. Might be related to continuous batching + different kernel mem alloc.

[03:40] Tom: can you remind us what the quant-kernel swap entailed? I think the SE notes said it swapped in 4-bit fused kernels?

[03:50] Priya: correct, fused 4-bit paths and an alternate attention fallback. In most cases cost drops ~20% but in sequences >1k tokens we saw extra GC-like stalls in GPU memory migration, which shows up as p99 blips.

[04:10] Ruth: that could be a showstopper if it affects interactive flows, our consumers will notice.

[04:25] Jordan: agreed — proposal is to run the e2e benchmark at simulated 1k concurrency to reproduce. If we see the spike, option A is kernel rollback for interactive routes only, option B is route-level config to cap sequence length and route long sequences to a dedicated model variant.

[04:50] Leah: second question on security — we need to enforce SAML SSO to access the Console and also require mTLS on the private plane endpoints. Is that supported?

[05:05] Priya: yes, Console SSO via SAML is supported; for private control plane endpoints we support TLS mutual auth and can integrate with customer CA or Redwood-managed certificates. KMS integration for model-store keys is implemented, HSM options are available for enterprise plans.

[05:30] Samir: for KMS can you clarify key rotation frequency and whether Redwood rotates keys on our behalf? Our compliance wants control.

[05:40] Carlos (CSM): most customers do customer-managed keys in the private offering; we can do dual-rotation or provide documented rotation windows, but default doesn't rotate customer keys without permission.

[06:00] Ruth: audit logs — we need retention of 1 year and an S3-compatible export with encryption at rest — is that standard?

[06:15] Priya: default is 90 days in the Console, we can configure longer retention in Private and push to your S3. We'll need the bucket ARN and policy, and we support SSE-KMS.

[06:35] Samir: back to networking — is there a recommended NAT configuration? We're currently running a single NAT GW per AZ; should we do multiple to avoid spikes?

[06:50] Priya: recommended is at least one NAT GW per AZ behind an ALB for egress scaling; also make sure route tables are explicit for peering connections. We'll send a best-practice diagram.

[07:10] Tom: the traces show some mis-attributed service names — sometimes the exporter labels a worker as "server-1-red" which makes triage slower. Any way to normalize that?

[07:22] Priya: yes we can push a tag mapping for the tracer and normalize the service_name at ingest; we'll include that in the telemetry patch.

[07:40] Ruth: what's the plan for the kernel upgrade? I want a low-risk schedule.

[07:50] Priya: plan: 1) Priya runs e2e benchmarks and pinpoints regression conditions, 2) if regression only affects long-seq routes we'll add route-level caps and keep kernel, 3) if regression is broader, roll back kernel for pilot and schedule deeper perf engineering work. Target canary date 2025-11-01 during a 2-hour window.

[08:20] Samir: can Redwood's fallback be configured to use a dedicated 'on-prem-only' model variant so there's no egress? We want fallback to be local-only for regulated tenants.

[08:35] Jordan: yes that's possible — route policy supports prefer-local, never-egress, and best-effort modes. We'll propose a route config and add the route_decision to audit logs.

[08:55] Leah: also need a signed attestation for SOC2 controls around log immutability and who can access keys.

[09:05] Carlos: we can share our SOC2 Type II report and the Private offering addendum; for attestation we can provide a statement of controls and engineer contact for deeper audit questions.

[09:25] Ruth: ok sounds good. two items from our side: we'll validate NAT headroom and send SAML metadata; also we'll prepare a short list of tenants that must never egress.

[09:45] Priya: perfect. I'll run the e2e and include both quant-kernel v1 and v2, and also include a run with KV-cache disabled to measure effect.

[10:05] Jordan: recap of decisions: 1) increase telemetry fields (add decision_id), 2) run 1k concurrency e2e, 3) we will propose route config to enforce never-egress for regulated tenants, 4) target narrow canary 2025-11-01. Any objections?

[10:30] Tom: no objections. one small ask — please include the raw flame graphs and p99 sample traces in the benchmark results.

[10:40] Priya: will do.

[10:48] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up via email and update the pilot tracker. Meeting end.

Notes: some transcript audio had crosstalk around 02:14 and 03:20 where words got garbled, see action items for clarification. References: shared deck: https://redwood.app/pilots/nimblehealth/telemetry-deck (internal link), benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/pilots/nimblehealth/benchmarks (internal link).
